summary.intent: Close two VERIFICATION.md gaps for CipherBox Phase 68 (rotation UX fail-closed gate + folderTree staleness), execute the fix plans, and then get the full local web-e2e Playwright suite running and passing to validate the phase end-to-end.
summary.outcome: Both gap-closure plans (68-11, 68-12) were planned, verified, executed, and phase-verified passing (SDK-tier tests green), but running the full web-e2e suite revealed the v2.0 web app's login→browse→download→upload flow is entirely stubbed with 'not implemented — phase 63/65' throws (46 stubs total); a new Phase 68.1 (Web Client Runtime Integration, 14 plans across 6 waves) was scoped, researched, planned, and plan-checker-verified (after one blocker/fix cycle) with full web-e2e-green as its exit gate, but execution was not started — plans are staged for user review.

repo: CipherBox v2.0 was built plumbing-first: sdk-core has complete read-chain (Phase 63) and write-chain (Phase 65) primitives, but the web app + client.ts wiring to those primitives was deliberately deferred and stubbed with 'not implemented — phase 63/65' throws — 17 read stubs + 29 write stubs = 46 total across apps/web/src and packages/sdk/src.

packages/sdk/src/client.ts `ensureFolderLoaded` (line ~478) is dead code that always throws 'not implemented — phase 63'; the real live pre-mutation chokepoint gating every rename/delete/deleteToBin/move is `reconcileFolderSequence` (client.ts:518, called at 5 sites: 742/823-824/985/1765).

packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/engine.ts `rotateReadFromNode` discarded the root's rotated {readKey, generation, sequenceNumber} behind a void return; its only production caller is client.ts:569 (performScopeExitRotation), making an additive RotateReadResult return backward-compatible.

packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts (~920 LOC) is the canonical, fully-implemented write-chain reference (createSharedSubfolder, uploadToSharedFolder, updateSharedFile, moveInSharedFolder, deleteFromSharedFolder, updateSharePermission) — owned-path equivalents are largely missing and must be built by copying this pattern.

Owned FolderState (packages/sdk/src/types.ts:164) is read-chain-only (no writeKey/publishedNode) while SharedFolderState (types.ts:205) carries a full write-body model; v3's SealedChildRef dropped ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted, so a recoverable subfolder writeKey can only live in a sealed write-body — forcing the owned model to be extended to match shared.

SealedChildRef (frozen v3 schema) has no `kind` field, so file-vs-folder discrimination requires either a network hop per child or a resolve-and-cache pattern at folder-load time — this is a real architecture decision, not just a stub to fill in.

apps/web has zero unit tests by design (SC#5 doctrine) — all web-tier logic verification goes through Playwright web-e2e; plans must include a verify command asserting no new apps/web/src/*.spec.ts files exist.

tests/web-e2e's Playwright `webServer` auto-starts mock-ipns-routing (:3001), API dev (:3000), and web dev (:5173), but Postgres, Kubo, and Redis must be provided externally, and BASE_URL in .env must point to localhost or Playwright skips starting the app servers.

The API's `nest start --watch` dev server has migrationsRun:true (synchronize off) so a fresh start auto-applies TypeORM migrations with no manual step; reusing a long-running watch process is safe if verified current (e.g. via a route-existence probe like `PATCH /shares/:id/grant` returning 401 not 404).

docs/TESTING.md doctrine: web-e2e execution is deferred to CI — a phase can be marked 'passed' with the durability spec merely authored, typecheck-clean, and registered (playwright test --list) rather than actually executed locally.

code.finding: reconcileFolderSequence is the correct live-reachability chokepoint for the ROT-07 fail-closed gate; the VERIFICATION.md-named ensureFolderLoaded is dead phase-63 stub code.
rotateReadFromNode's DFS/BFS child-resolve pattern (resolveAndFetch + unsealChildReadKey) is the template used for building ensureFolderLoaded's real implementation.

New-user login throws 'not implemented — phase 63' when trying to publish the root Node, blocking all downstream login-dependent web-e2e specs; introduced in commit b2dba554a (Phase 62), not by Phase 68 work.
createFileMetadata and updateFileMetadata are the root blockers for owned file upload/replace/versions — genuinely missing (not just unwired), must be built from the shared-write.ts pattern.
collectChildKeys subtree re-wrap is the core blocker for share creation and invite creation on the write side; depends on the read-chain being wired first.

workflow: For gap-closure planning, spawning the planner with the VERIFICATION.md gaps plus explicit instructions to append new plans (never overwrite existing ones) and serialize shared-file edits across sequential waves prevents merge collisions.

The plan-checker agent independently re-verifies source-grounded substitutions (e.g. confirming a dead-code target vs a live chokepoint) rather than trusting the planner's claim — caught a real wiring gap (kind-cache defined but never invoked) that would have silently broken file rendering.
A 'GSD commit-helper false negative' pattern recurs: the tool reports commit_failed while the commit actually lands — verify via `git log` rather than retrying.
Using `gsd-tools phase insert` (decimal phase numbering, e.g. 68.1) to slot new scope between existing phases avoids renumbering ~15 cross-references to a downstream phase (FUSE at 69).

Reporting exit code 0 from a background wrapper script can be misleading if the wrapper's own final echo succeeds even when the wrapped command (Playwright) failed — must check the actual suite summary/log, not just the wrapper's exit code.

When reusing a long-running dev server for e2e rather than restarting it, verify it reflects current source (e.g. hitting a known-new route and confirming 401 not 404) rather than assuming freshness from process age.

friction: Running the full web-e2e suite required significant manual environment archaeology (CI workflow, README, playwright config, .env files, docker ps, port conflicts) before it could even be attempted.

Reused a stale 18h-old API build on :3000 that predated the current source; had to detect and route around it, including discovering the port was immediately reclaimed by a watch-mode dev server after being killed.

First full suite run misleadingly reported 'test-login failed (401)' which looked like a stale-secret issue but was a red herring — the real, dominant failure was every login-dependent test timing out on page navigation due to an unrelated stub.
Wrapper script exit code (0) did not reflect actual Playwright suite pass/fail (1), requiring a second read of the log to find the true result.

The scope of 'make web-e2e pass' ballooned mid-session from what looked like a rotation-suite check into an entire missing phase of work (46 runtime stubs, read + write chain), discovered only after two sequential deep-inventory subagent dispatches.
Plan-checker caught a blocker (kind-cache built but never wired into any render path) that would have silently broken all file recognition in the UI had it shipped as originally planned.
open_items: Phase 68.1 (Web Client Runtime Integration) plans 01–14 are fully planned and plan-checker-verified but not yet executed — user must approve before `/gsd-execute-phase 68.1`.

Two design decisions were resolved by the planner and flagged for user review: D-02 (kind discrimination via an in-memory resolve-and-cache) and D-03 (extending owned FolderState to carry a write-body like SharedFolderState).

4 pre-existing todos tagged `resolves_phase: 68` were deliberately NOT auto-closed since none were actually resolved by the gap-closure work — they need retagging to a rotation-hardening/write-plane phase (rotation-concurrent-add-merge-downgrades, rotation-fresh-record-resume, rotation-coderabbit-followups-deferred, phase68-shared-write-context-publishednode-wiring).
The deferred CannotWriteUntilRefetchError finding (Phase 65/66 WRITE-03/04) remains explicitly out of scope and carried forward as `deferred`.
